name: Ashok Leyland Ltd.
business_summary: Hinduja-group maker of medium and heavy commercial vehicles (M&HCV), LCVs, buses, defence vehicles, engines and spares; also Switch Mobility (EV) and a captive financing associate. FY26 sales Rs44,007 cr, TTM EBITDA margin 12.8%, PAT Rs3,581 cr; Q1 FY27 sales Rs9,634 cr, EBITDA 10%, PAT Rs609 cr, record volume 48,763 units. Almost debt-free, ROE 30%, dividend yield 2.1%. Market cap Rs100,472 cr at 26x P/E. Cyclical: volumes follow GDP, freight, infrastructure and financing conditions. Segment mix is model knowledge.

revenue_mix.segment: spares, engines, power solutions, Switch EV

exposures.mechanism: M&HCV volumes are ~2.5-3x GDP-cyclical (freight tonnage, mining, construction). +1pp GDP => ~+4% industry volume; operating leverage ~2x on 13% margin => EBITDA +8%; x EV/MCap 1.0 x persistence 0.5 => ~+4, shaded to 3.5. Oct 2026 sales +23% to 21,888 units, Sep +28% to 24,049 (record Q1 volume 48,763).

evidence.note: Financial Express: CV volumes record 48,763 units in Q1; Upstox: EBITDA margin impacted by rising material costs

exposures.mechanism: Tippers, haulers and construction trucks follow road/rail/mining capex. +10% capex growth => ~+4% volume in ~35% of CV segments => ~+1.5% total volume, x2 operating leverage => EBITDA +3%, plus sentiment and state-capex timing; central +3.0.
Road construction drives tipper and multi-axle demand (~25% of M&HCV); +10% roads spend => ~+2.5% volumes => ~+1.5 after persistence 0.5.

Steel (sheet, forgings, castings) ~15% of costs. +7% => cost base Rs39,185 cr x 15% x 7% = ~Rs410 cr = ~7% of EBITDA Rs5,732 cr; ~50% recovered through price hikes with lag => -3.6% EBITDA x persistence 0.5 x EV/MCap 1.0 => -1.8. Q1 FY27 margin fell ~1pt on material costs (Economic Times 2026-08-18). Global HRC +20.6% since June signals ongoing pressure.

evidence.note: Economic Times: record June quarter, margin fell a full point

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium (castings, radiators) ~3% of costs; +10% => +0.3% costs => ~-2% EBITDA, half recovered, persistence 0.5 => -0.5; empirical -1.62 (t=-1.8) is larger, so central shaded to -0.9.
Tyres (rubber-linked) ~5% of costs; +10% rubber => ~+0.4% costs => ~-1.7% EBITDA, partial pass-through => ~-0.7 after persistence.

Diesel is the largest operating cost for fleet owners (~50-60% of running cost), so +10% Brent compresses operator margins, delays fleet replacement and hurts used-CV values; also raises India inflation and eases around EV transition. Empirical -1.52 per SSU, t=-2.8 (strong) matches. Crude's 5 Nov fall helped the stock (Business Standard headline 'TaMo CV, Ashok Leyland, Maruti rally up to 8% as crude tumbles').

evidence.note: Business Standard: rally as crude oil price tumbles (headline)

exposures.mechanism: ~90% of CVs are financed; +25bp raises EMI ~0.3% and dealer/fleet funding cost (company itself is nearly debt-free, interest Rs169 cr). RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07 and auto stocks fell (CNBC TV18 2026-10-07). Includes discount-rate effect at 26x P/E.

evidence.note: Google News: Reuters 2026-10-07 'India first hike in nearly 4 years'; SCC Online 'repo to 5.50%, calibrated tightening'

exposures.mechanism: CRIF (Business Standard 2026-08-19) flags CV loan stress; +50bp credit costs tightens NBFC CV lending (and hits the Hinduja Leyland Finance associate). Equity impact via volumes ~-1% and associate earnings.
Exports ~10-12% of volume (Middle East, Africa, SAARC; model knowledge) vs imported electronics/components; net small positive. +3% => ~+0.3.
Switch Mobility electric buses/LCVs benefit from PM e-Bus Sewa/PM E-DRIVE subsidies; EV business still loss-making so valuation impact modest.
Gulf is a key export region (UAE, Saudi) and escalation lifts Brent/diesel; both reduce demand. Partially double-counted with F_BRENT so shaded.
